page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server instance featuring 288 vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64 and includes a 504 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 1080 GB of DDR5 RAM running at 6 GHz, providing 3.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of six NVMe SSDs totaling 16,242 GB. No GPU accelerators are present.

Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, reaching 22,887.6 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and over 1,086 GB/sec for large-block reads. Database operations, Redis SET operations at 401.21 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput at 161.59 GB/sec also rank in the top tier. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench image processing scores falling into the middle 50% average.

While prompt processing for medium 7B LLM models ranks in the top 10%, text generation for small 135M models is poor, placing in the bottom 10%. This indicates a tradeoff where the architecture excels at high-throughput parallel processing and memory-bound operations but is less efficient for specific low-parameter sequential generation tasks. Given the massive local NVMe storage, high memory bandwidth, and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this server is suited for large-scale database hosting, high-throughput web serving, cryptography, and parallel software compilation.
